name: Roman Imperial
period: 27 BCE–late 5th century CE in western framing; vary by region and century
region: Roman Empire; Italy and provincial contexts
summary: Imperial-period portraiture ranges from idealized dynastic images to highly individualized likenesses; architecture, dress and hairstyle change substantially across centuries.

wardrobe.text: toga/stola/tunic/armor only when role and context justify them

hairstyle_headwear.text: portrait hairstyle is highly date-sensitive and useful for narrowing chronology

architecture.text: forum, basilica, domus/villa, baths, streets or provincial settings by context

interior_furniture.text: marble/painted plaster/mosaic and wooden furnishings by status/context

transportation.text: walking, horse, cart/chariot, ship depending on role

writing_calligraphy.text: Latin/Greek inscriptions when verified; avoid pseudo-Latin filler if text is meant to be read

lighting_technology.text: oil lamps and daylight in interiors

incompatible_or_anachronistic.text: Renaissance neoclassical costume presented as Roman evidence
Classical Greek nudity rules copied blindly into Roman portrait context

prompt_fragments.bust: Build a materially credible Roman portrait bust: intentional truncation and support, period-sensitive hair, modeled flesh/hair contrast, and either idealized or individualized likeness chosen from the narrative—not both accidentally.

sources.supports: Roman bronze bust, date-sensitive hair/toga, individual characterization
bronze as a valued Roman honorific portrait medium and fidelity to nature

scope_note: Foundation pack: use as a bounded starting point, not an encyclopedia.
strict_reconstruction_note: Strict mode should narrow century/reign, province, status, and portrait convention.
